title: conversation-slab-sweep-lab-notes-jun15-2029
content:
Purpose:
Quick lab notes from the Conversation Slab sweep we ran to sanity-check slab sizing heuristics against a mixed conversational workload. This is intentionally informal — raw numbers, ASCII plots, and immediate takeaways so SE/Platform can iterate on slab sizing rules before we turn this into a proper runbook.

Context / why: 
- Product asked whether current slab default (4-concurrency small-session slab) is over-provisioned for conversational microbursts seen in customer demos.
- Hypothesis: modestly wider slabs (6–8) reduce tail P99 for short convo turns with small token outputs while improving amortized cost per session; but they might increase cold-start penalty for sparse long-turn sessions.

Test matrix (short):
- Model: open-llm-v2-13B (quantized 4-bit profile used in Dedicated test pool)
- HW: A100-40GB equivalent (internal cluster bench nodes: a100b-40-spot-12)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v2.8.3 + slab-scheduler prototype (branch: slab-sweep-jun2029)
- Workloads: three synthetic mixes derived from production traces (week of 2029-05):
  * mix-A (micro): 80% short turns (<=20 tokens), 20% medium turns (21-80), bursty arrival (lambda spikes)
  * mix-B (balanced): 40% short, 40% medium, 20% long (>80 tokens)
  * mix-C (longy): 70% long turns, 30% medium, rare bursts
- Slab widths tested: 2, 4 (baseline), 6, 8
- Session affordance: session pinning enabled for app-id tag, prefetch disabled (to isolate slab impact)
- Duration per run: 30 minutes steady-state + 15 minutes warmup

Measurement knobs:
- Reported metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency per response (endpoint RT from request->first-byte), amortized $/session (estimated compute cost using internal pricing model), slab utilization (slot occupancy), cold-start ratio (requests that triggered a new slab instance), and tail jitter (measured as p99-p95).
- Sampling: 1s granularity time series, per-minute aggregations for ascii-summaries.

ASCII micro-summary (mix-A, snapshot -- steady-state minutes 10–20):
- mean slot occupancy: 0.62
- cold-start-ratio: 0.04
- p50/p95/p99 (ms): 48 / 130 / 360

Slab width sweep (mix-A):
- slab=2   | slot-occupancy=0.39 | p50=44  p95=160 p99=520 | $/session=0.0038 | cold=0.11
- slab=4   | slot-occupancy=0.57 | p50=46  p95=140 p99=380 | $/session=0.0031 | cold=0.06
- slab=6   | slot-occupancy=0.68 | p50=49  p95=125 p99=300 | $/session=0.0028 | cold=0.03
- slab=8   | slot-occupancy=0.71 | p50=51  p95=122 p99=290 | $/session=0.0027 | cold=0.02

Quick interpret (mix-A):
- Going from 2->6 materially reduced tail latency (p99 520 -> 300ms) and reduced amortized cost by ~26% per session because compute packing improved.
- Diminishing returns after 6: 6->8 gave modest p99 improvement (~10%) but cost delta small. Slot occupancy rising above ~0.7 suggests risk of headroom loss under heavier bursts.

ASCII micro-summary (mix-C, steady-state minutes 10–20):
- mean slot occupancy: 0.28
- cold-start-ratio: 0.03
- p50/p95/p99 (ms): 220 / 540 / 1100

Slab width sweep (mix-C):
- slab=2   | slot-occupancy=0.16 | p50=210 p95=560 p99=1120 | $/session=0.0120 | cold=0.02
- slab=4   | slot-occupancy=0.27 | p50=225 p95=540 p99=1110 | $/session=0.0116 | cold=0.03
- slab=6   | slot-occupancy=0.31 | p50=240 p95=545 p99=1100 | $/session=0.0115 | cold=0.04
- slab=8   | slot-occupancy=0.32 | p50=245 p95=548 p99=1095 | $/session=0.0114 | cold=0.05

Quick interpret (mix-C):
- For long-turn dominated traffic, wider slabs don't buy much for tail latency because individual requests consume slots for longer duration; occupancy remains low and amortized cost per session largely driven by token compute.
- Cold-start ratio increases slightly with wider slabs due to fewer slabs fitting onto a node when active long sessions monopolize resources — this increases instance churn.

Balanced mix-B notes:
- Behavior sits between A and C. Optimal slab width for balanced workload looks like 4 or 6 depending on SLA: if P99 target < 400ms choose 6; if cost sensitivity higher pick 4.

Tail-jitter tradeoff (p99-p95):
- mix-A: slab=2 -> jitter=360ms; slab=6 -> jitter=175ms (improvement)
- mix-C: slab=2 -> jitter=560ms; slab=6 -> jitter=555ms (no real improvement)

Actionable takeaways (short):
1) Default slab width: change baseline from 4 -> 6 in the SLAB-DEFAULT policy only for "conversation-microburst" workload class (heuristic: short-turn fraction >=60% and burstiness>0.6). Put behind an opt-in toggle for Dedicated customers initially.
2) Add slab-adaptation metric to Console: show short-turn fraction per app and recommended slab width with expected $/session delta. (Ticket: JIRA-OBS-3142)
3) For long-session heavy apps, keep default at 4 and recommend session pinning + prefetch options rather than slab widening.
4) Run a 24h soak of slab=6 vs slab=4 in staging using real customer traces to capture diurnal patterns and verify instance churn/cost implications.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Warmup penalty interactions: in some runs we saw brief p99 spikes at minute 2–3 when many sessions started concurrently. Need to instrument whether slot preemption or kernel compilation caused this.
- Multi-model nodes: we only bench single-model pools. How do slabs interact when node has multiple co-located models with different token length distributions?
- Pricing model sensitivity: our $/session estimate assumes steady A100 pricing; need a quick sensitivity sweep for cheaper ephemeral GPU classes (e.g., L40x) to see if slab recommendations change.

Notes on methodology caveats:
- These are lab runs on a dedicated bench fleet; production noise and network variance can shift absolute p99 numbers by +/- 10–20%.
- Tokenization differences and prompt templates in real apps may change short-turn fraction; recommend conservative thresholding for automatic policy changes.

Immediate next steps (owner names):
- Marcus Chen: wire slab-suggestion metric into runtime telemetry dashboard (ETA 2w).
- Aditi Kapoor: run 24h soak (staging) using customer trace sample set-2029-05 (ETA 1w to start, report in 10 days).
- Lena Rivera: add short writeup to Console team GH issue with ASCII charts and draft recommended defaults (this doc).

Appendix: raw ascii time-sample (mix-A, slab=6 minutes 12-16)
[time] occupancy | p95(ms)
12:00  | 0.63      | 132
12:01  | 0.71      | 128
12:02  | 0.66      | 126
12:03  | 0.69      | 122
12:04  | 0.64      | 136

End of lab notes.
If we decide to iterate on policy, I'll fold these into a formal runbook with parameter knobs and expected regression windows.
